interface.name: org_kde_kwin_blur_manager
interface.description: This interface allows a client to request blur effect for a surface.

request.name: create

description.summary: create a blur object for a surface

request.description: Create a blur object for a surface.

request.name: unset
request.description: Remove blur effect from a surface.

interface.name: org_kde_kwin_blur
interface.description: This interface allows a client to specify a blur region for a surface.

request.name: commit
request.description: Apply all the previously configured state for this blur object.

request.name: set_region
request.description: Set the blur region. If region is null, the entire surface will be blurred.

request.name: release
request.description: Release the blur object, removing the blur effect from the surface.

request.name: set_radius
request.description: Set the blur radius in pixels. If not set, the compositor's default blur radius is used. The value is a fixed-point number with 8 bits of fractional precision (i.e. multiply the desired radius by 256). For example, a 2px blur is 512, a 60px blur is 15360.

request.name: set_saturation
request.description: Set the saturation applied to the blurred backdrop, matching CSS `backdrop-filter: saturate(x)`. 1.0 leaves saturation unchanged, values above 1.0 increase it, below 1.0 desaturate. If not set, the compositor applies no saturation change. The value is a fixed-point number with 8 bits of fractional precision (i.e. multiply the desired multiplier by 256). For example, saturate(1.0) is 256, saturate(1.3) is 332, saturate(2.0) is 512.

request.name: set_tint
request.description: Set how strongly the compositor blends a white overlay onto the blurred backdrop (the "frosted glass" lightening). 0.0 disables the tint so the backdrop is a faithful `backdrop-filter: blur()` and the surface's own background provides the glass colour; higher values add more white. If not set, the compositor default tint is used. The value is a fixed-point number with 8 bits of fractional precision (multiply by 256). For example, 0.0 is 0, the default 0.15 is 38, full white is 256.

request.name: set_border
request.description: Set the alpha of the compositor's 1px frosted-glass border drawn around the blurred backdrop. 0.0 disables the border entirely (useful when the surface draws its own border client-side); the compositor default is roughly 0.2. If not set, the compositor default border is used. The value is a fixed-point number with 8 bits of fractional precision (multiply by 256). For example, 0.0 is 0, 0.2 is 51.

request.name: set_region_radii

description.summary: set per-rectangle corner radii for the blur region

request.description:
Set the corner radii of the individual rectangles of the blur region, so a surface can round each backdrop to the shape it actually draws there. Without this the compositor rounds every rectangle of the region with a single radius, which is wrong for any surface that draws different shapes in different rectangles — e.g. a fully rounded pill alongside cards with a smaller radius.
The argument is an array of 32-bit unsigned integers, four per rectangle — top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, in surface-local logical pixels — ordered to match the rectangles added to the wl_region passed to set_region. Rectangles without a corresponding entry (a shorter array) keep the compositor's single-radius behaviour, so a client may supply radii for a prefix of the region. A trailing partial quadruple is ignored.
A radius larger than half of the rectangle's shorter side is clamped to it, so a very large value yields a fully rounded ("pill") rectangle whatever its size.
The radii pair with the region committed in the same cycle: like set_region, this is pending state applied on the next commit, and the two requests may be sent in either order within a cycle. A commit that carries a region but no radii rounds every rectangle the old way.

arg.name: radii
arg.summary: four uint32 radii (tl, tr, br, bl) per region rectangle

request.name: set_region_geometry

description.summary: set the exact sub-pixel geometry of the blur region

request.description:
Set the exact geometry of the individual rectangles of the blur region, with sub-pixel precision.
A wl_region carries whole logical pixels, but a surface does not generally draw on whole logical pixels: a card laid out from measured text, or one under a scale animation, sits at a fractional position and size. The compositor must therefore round the region to something, and whichever way it rounds is visible — rounding out lets the backdrop escape past the shape the client draws over it, and rounding in leaves the client's own translucent border with no backdrop beneath it. Neither is correctable by the client, because the client cannot express what it means.
This request carries that missing precision. The wl_region rectangles remain the conservative whole-pixel bound the compositor uses for capture, clipping and damage; the geometry given here is the exact area the effect is rendered to, and must be contained by its region rectangle. A compositor clamps it if it is not.
The argument is an array of 32-bit signed integers, four per rectangle — x, y, width, height, in surface-local logical pixels as fixed-point numbers with 8 bits of fractional precision (multiply by 256) — ordered to match the rectangles added to the wl_region passed to set_region. Rectangles without a corresponding entry (a shorter array) use their whole-pixel region rectangle unchanged, so a client may supply geometry for a prefix of the region. A trailing partial quadruple is ignored.
The geometry pairs with the region committed in the same cycle: like set_region, this is pending state applied on the next commit, and the two requests may be sent in either order within a cycle. A commit that carries a region but no geometry uses the region rectangles as-is, exactly as version 4 did.

arg.name: geometry
arg.summary: four fixed-point int32 (x, y, width, height) per region rectangle
